# Program Structure {#sec-structure}

Part II describes what the program does with the model of Part I. Statements
about *numerical devices* are explicitly marked as such: they change the path of the
iteration or the quality of the mesh, but are not derived from the energy.

The code is split into two Python distributions. **DropletRelaxer** is the
headless solver: it depends on NumPy, SciPy and h5py only, reads a scenario
(a TOML file, @sec-usage-configuration) and writes a run file
(@sec-file-format). **DropletViewer** reads run files, or runs the solver in the
same process with a live window; it depends on DropletRelaxer, PyVista and VTK.
The solver never imports the viewer.

```
  scenario.toml ──► droplet-relax (DropletRelaxer.driver) ──► run.h5 (VTKHDF + /DropletRelaxer)
                                                                   │
                       ParaView / any VTK ◄────────────────────────┤
                       droplet-view (replay, --follow, --video) ◄──┘
  scenario.toml ──► droplet-view live  =  driver + H5Writer + LiveWindow in one process
```

::: {#tbl-modules}
| Module | Content |
|:---|:---|
| `DropletRelaxer.config` | All parameters (dataclasses `MeshConfig`, `SolverConfig`, `ObstacleConfig`, `OutputConfig`, `AnomalyConfig`, `RoughnessConfig`, `QuasiStaticConfig`); strict TOML loading, overrides, volume scaling. |
| `DropletRelaxer.driver` | Start mesh, scaling to the target volume, remesh scheduling, frames and checkpoints for the sinks, restart. |
| `DropletRelaxer.mesh` | Start meshes, DOF mask, global subdivision, Rivara refinement, edge collapse, tangential smoothing. |
| `DropletRelaxer.substrate` | Closed mesh: base triangulation (Tutte embedding / ear clipping), per-triangle energy weights. |
| `DropletRelaxer.energy` | Area, volume and their gradients, graph Laplacian, curvature, wall energy, substrate penetration, centre of mass. |
| `DropletRelaxer.obstacle` | Straight sphere path $\mathbf c(u)$, collision/adhesion penalty. |
| `DropletRelaxer.quasistatic` | Event-driven sphere stepping: convergence test, step advance, adaptive rollback, ETA. |
| `DropletRelaxer.wetting` | Wetted-set detection, contact loop, sphere wetting energy. |
| `DropletRelaxer.anomaly` | Circular wettability anomaly (polygon flux and exact gradient). |
| `DropletRelaxer.roughness` | Random substrate roughness / chemical disorder. |
| `DropletRelaxer.solver` | The relaxation generator `relax`, force on the sphere, step control. |
| `DropletRelaxer.analysis` | Per-frame quantities: surface free energy, COM offset, gap. |
| `DropletRelaxer.io` | `Frame`, `FrameSink`, `StopRequest`; the run file (`schema`, `writer`, `reader`). |
| `DropletRelaxer.cli` | `droplet-relax run`, `restart`, `info`, `show-config`. |
| `DropletViewer.scene` | Window, surface, sphere, contact lines, substrate, info texts, progress bar. |
| `DropletViewer.charts`, `.history`, `.video` | Energy and force charts, history slider with Play/Save, video export. |
| `DropletViewer.live` | `LiveWindow`, the in-process live window as a frame sink. |
| `DropletViewer.app`, `.cli` | `droplet-view` (replay, `--follow`, `--video`, `live`). |

: Modules of the program.
:::

**Data flow.** `DropletRelaxer.driver.Driver` builds and scales the start
mesh, then runs `DropletRelaxer.solver.relax`, a Python generator that performs
iterations and yields every state to the driver. The driver decides on
remeshing; when a remesh trigger fires, the segment ends, the mesh is changed
and a new `relax` segment continues at the same iteration number. Everything the
outputs need is computed by the driver (`DropletRelaxer.analysis`) and handed to
*frame sinks*: a read-only `Frame` per recorded state, `Event`s (remesh,
divergence, log lines), a cheap `tick` per iteration and periodic restart
checkpoints. The HDF5 writer, the console output and the live window are such
sinks. Nothing flows back into the numerics except a `StopRequest` (window
closed, Stop button, SIGTERM), so a run is bit-identical with or without a
window.
